title: How ast-grep Rewrote Tree-sitter in Rust and Made It 30% Faster
excerpt: The complete adventure of using AI to rewrite Tree-sitter's C core in Rust, simplify it, optimize it, and discover that a faster parser could still make ast-grep slower.
content_html:
Part 1 of 4 — the complete adventure

ast-grep rewrote Tree-sitter's C core in Rust, with AI writing the code. The new core is faster at parsing, faster at reading the completed tree, and faster in ast-grep itself. (The title's “30%” is the parser-only number; end-to-end, ast-grep runs about 22% faster.)

Source repository: HerringtonDarkholme/tree-sitter.

Two quick introductions before the numbers. ast-grep — the structural code-search tool this blog belongs to — searches code by syntax rather than by text, so every file it touches must first become a syntax tree. Tree-sitter is the parser framework that builds that tree: you give it a grammar definition, and it generates a fast parser for that language. Born in the editor world, it now powers an enormous ecosystem of grammars and tools.

Performance and peak RSS. Throughput is normalized so the unmodified C build (“C / normal”) scores 100; higher is better. RSS is peak resident memory, and the raw-parsing row shows it as a range because it varies across the benchmark's language fixtures. The outline row is ast-grep's real workload: parse every file in a repository, then walk each completed tree to extract a structural outline.

Rust won every parser and traversal fixture, and ast-grep produced exactly the same outline. Memory is the tradeoff: the Rust build uses about 8 MiB more in the ast-grep run. On the much larger TypeScript stress corpus — the TypeScript compiler repository's test-baseline tree, this project's memory torture test — it peaks at 91.2 MiB. That figure is a triumph, not a confession: earlier in the project, the same corpus peaked above 1 GiB.

The result is not a 1:1 replacement for upstream Tree-sitter. It is a narrower runtime built for AI coding agents that analyze complete file snapshots:

  • Existing generated languages and parsers remain compatible.
  • Native loading of WebAssembly-compiled languages and incremental old-tree reuse were removed.
  • Compatibility still requires many raw pointers and unsafe blocks.

That boundary keeps the grammar ecosystem useful for agentic coding while removing editor-specific machinery the target workload does not need.

That is the ending. Getting there was another matter.

Why Rewrite Tree-sitter? ​

Every serious ast-grep performance investigation eventually arrived at the same place: Tree-sitter.

ast-grep could make its rules faster. It could prune work, cache configuration, and avoid visiting irrelevant syntax. But every file still had to become a syntax tree first, and Tree-sitter built that tree. The parser was both the foundation and, increasingly, the ceiling.

I had dreamed about rewriting or deeply optimizing it for years. The dream usually lasted until I opened the runtime. There was a mature C implementation, binary compatibility, external scanners, error recovery, incremental parsing, ambiguous grammars, several language bindings, and a small matter of not breaking the enormous grammar ecosystem built on top of all of it.

For one person, this was not a weekend project. It was a Herculean task wearing a header file.

So nothing happened.

Then AI-assisted rewrite attempts started appearing everywhere—Bun, pgrust, and Roc among them. They did not prove that rewriting Tree-sitter was wise, make the runtime smaller, or make parser theory less strange. They showed that the experiment had become cheap enough for one person to attempt, giving me enough leverage to ask the unreasonable question and get an answer before the decade ended.

So I instructed ChatGPT to rewrite Tree-sitter's C core in Rust. The project moved from a compatibility-first translation, through a fast but unreadable optimization attempt, to a simpler runtime and real parser gains—only to discover that a faster parser could still make ast-grep slower.

The rest of this post follows that journey: what worked, what had to be reverted, and what it took to turn a parser benchmark win into an application win.

Tree-sitter's Parsing Architecture ​

Tree-sitter takes source code and produces a syntax tree. Each supported language begins as a grammar definition that Tree-sitter compiles into generated parsing tables and lexer code; when this series says “generated languages,” “generated grammars,” or “generated tables,” it means those artifacts. At runtime, a lexer turns characters into tokens such as identifier, +, and number. The parser then uses the generated table and a stack to decide what each token means.

Most of the time, the table requests one of two operations:

  • shift: consume a token and push it onto the parser stack;
  • reduce: recognize that several syntax pieces form a larger grammar rule, replace them with one parent, and continue.

If every table entry had one valid answer, the parser could follow one history with one stack. That is the ordinary LR case. Programming-language grammars occasionally have genuine conflicts: more than one action may remain valid until additional input reveals which interpretation survives.

Tree-sitter therefore uses generalized LR (GLR). It can follow several histories at once while sharing their common past in a graph-structured stack. Think of one road that can briefly fork, then merge again. The graph is necessary when the grammar is ambiguous. It is considerably less charming when the parser constructs graph machinery for a road that remains straight.

The other central object is the subtree. A shifted token becomes a leaf; a reduction combines children into an internal syntax node. These values are created during parsing, shared across stack histories, published as the final tree, traversed by ast-grep, and eventually released. Optimizing only their birth while ignoring the rest of that lifetime would later produce a rather expensive lesson.

That is enough parser theory for the overview.

First Step: Preserve C Behavior in Rust ​

The first goal was not elegance. It was parity.

The rewrite contract was deliberately conservative:

  • Use the existing tests as the behavioral oracle. A plausible Rust implementation was not enough; it had to produce the same trees, recovery behavior, navigation results, and public API effects.
  • Test the ecosystem, not only handwritten examples. Existing generated grammars and external scanners had to keep working without regeneration or source changes.
  • Preserve the binary interface (ABI). Generated language tables, public C functions, layouts, symbols, and calling conventions remained compatible while the implementation behind them changed language.
  • Translate before redesigning. The first Rust version intentionally resembled the C control flow so parity failures had a bounded search area.

In one sentence: preserve everything the ecosystem can observe, then make the inside replaceable.

I instructed ChatGPT to translate the runtime one part at a time: basic utilities, tree storage, lexing, the parser stack, tree navigation, and finally the parser loop. The agent read the C and Rust code, wrote patches, fixed compiler errors, ran tests, and investigated mismatches. I supplied the goals, constraints, objections, and decisions. The existing implementation and test suite supplied the answer key.

This distinction matters. I did not personally type a heroic Rust port and then ask AI to polish the comments. The implementation, profiling, instrumentation, and much of the experimental code were produced by the agent under my direction. Without AI, this project would still be an idea I occasionally mentioned before wisely changing the subject.

The C core had become Rust. It compiled. It passed the tests. Existing grammars could use it. This was already the kind of result that had looked impossible when the project was sitting on the shelf.

Naturally, I immediately asked for more.

Why the First Optimization Attempt Failed ​

The request was pure vibe coding — one line typed into a /goal command. The process behind it was more careful than that: I directed ChatGPT to use proper profiling tools, understand the runtime's data layouts and ownership, and look for algorithmic changes instead of merely polishing individual instructions. The benchmarks duly crossed the requested line. Then I opened the code and could not follow it. Layers of overlapping AI-generated optimizations sat on top of a mechanical C-to-Rust translation, and soon the parser began segfaulting: no friendly Rust panic, no failed assertion, the process simply left. A parser that is twenty percent faster and occasionally disappears is not an optimization. It is a benchmark with a jump scare.

I reverted the optimization work entirely. The twenty percent went with it, and the performance the project eventually reached came later, from the clean, layered work described below. Part 2 tells this story in full. What matters here is how it reversed the project: I stopped asking ChatGPT to make the pile faster and started asking it to make the system explainable.

Second Step: Reduce Scope and Improve Readability ​

The cleanup had two parts:

  1. delete features and representations outside the target product;
  2. turn the retained C-style Rust into code whose ownership and control flow could be reasoned about locally.

Neither step promised a heroic benchmark. Both were prerequisites for trusting the next one.

Remove Incremental Parsing from the Target Runtime ​

At first, “rewrite Tree-sitter” implied preserving every feature. Then the target workload forced a better question: preserving it for whom?

Upstream Tree-sitter is famously useful inside editors. A human inserts one character, deletes two more, and expects highlighting to update before the next frame. Incremental parsing lets the runtime reuse the old tree and rebuild only the affected region. In that world, reparsing the complete file after every keystroke is needless work.

That was not the world of this branch. ast-grep and the AI coding-agent tools I cared about operate on complete file snapshots: an agent reads a file, analyzes or rewrites it, and asks the tool to process the new snapshot. There is no editor-owned syntax tree advancing one keystroke at a time. A fresh parse is not a degraded fallback; it is the normal operation.

So I decided to remove incremental old-tree reuse and instructed ChatGPT to do it. The public parameter remains for compatibility, but this runtime parses fresh. The machinery for finding and reusing pieces of the old tree — and it reached into a surprising number of core structures — disappeared from the hot implementation; Part 2 inventories exactly what went.

A second, separate scope cut rode along with it: native loading of Wasm-compiled grammars. Tree-sitter can compile a grammar to WebAssembly and load it at runtime — a capability distinct from the browser Wasm build, which stayed. Native tools set this project's performance target, and runtime Wasm grammar loading was not part of that workload.

This is not a proposal that upstream Tree-sitter should abandon incremental parsing. It is a product decision for a narrower runtime aimed at file-at-a-time analysis and agent tooling. If this branch returns to interactive editor use, the decision must be reopened. That was the rule: delete only behind a declared boundary, never because a feature happened to be inconvenient.

Deletion turned out to be the first real optimization technique: remove work whose use case has already left the building.

Refactor the Retained Runtime for Maintainability ​

A line-by-line translation is only readable if the reader already knows the original line by line. I instructed ChatGPT to break the monolithic, pointer-heavy port into more idiomatic internal Rust—without making the ABI-facing types “idiomatic” in ways that would break existing grammars.

The cleanup was less a redesign than a long series of small promotions. Internal raw-pointer parameters became references or slices wherever their lifetimes were local and provable; a sentinel pointer meaning “no node here” became an honest Option. Out-parameters turned into return values where the C ABI did not demand them, large modules split by responsibility so mutation sat next to the state it changed, and the dense tricks that had to stay — compact indexes into the tree, pointer arithmetic — were hidden behind narrow, named operations. Where compatibility was real, the code stayed deliberately ugly: generated-language layouts and exported functions remained C-shaped, because another binary had already committed to that shape.

That cleanup made questions answerable: Who owns this piece of the tree? Can this reference survive when its storage grows? Why does one reduction create a temporary parser state only to delete it immediately?

The important output was not prettier syntax. It was a runtime organized well enough that a segfault, invariant failure, or suspicious allocation had an address in the architecture.

GLR and Memory-Layout Optimizations ​

Once I could understand the runtime, I directed ChatGPT back toward reduction — the “reduce” from the architecture section above, and the operation the parser performs constantly.

That small operation touches both major data structures. It removes the children from the parser's working stack, then stores them under a new parent in the syntax tree. The profile showed that Tree-sitter was doing much more work around those children than the ordinary case required.

The successful changes eventually fell into four simple principles:

  • Avoid work for uncommon cases. About 99% of the observed parser stack was one straight path, so the parser no longer builds a graph until the input actually forks. Work needed mainly for editing is also kept out of a fresh parse when possible.
  • Make allocation cheap, and indexes small. Asking the general-purpose allocator for every internal syntax node is expensive. An arena obtains a growing block and serves many nodes from it. Separately, compact indexes reduce the bytes moved between the parser stack and the tree.
  • Do repeated work once. The parser prepares common grammar lookups ahead of time, and the tree reader avoids looking up the same children repeatedly.
  • Give the simplest cases a short path. One parser action is handled directly, and ordinary ASCII input avoids the full character-decoding path. The complete fallback remains available whenever the simple path does not apply.

text

ordinary parse: keep one stack path
real ambiguity: switch to the full graph

The 99% number described the problem, but not the solution. I directed ChatGPT (in research mode rather than coding mode, this time) to review academic work on generalized parsers, and the result pointed to an older lesson: do not build the general structure until the input actually needs it. The arena was a separate idea and required its own experiments. The linear stack avoided graph bookkeeping; the arena reduced calls to the general allocator. Making the indexes smaller was yet another layout choice, and it did not become faster automatically. Several versions lost before the pieces paid for themselves.

The important result: ordinary parsing stopped paying the full price of rare ambiguity and of separate allocation for every internal syntax node.

For a moment, the parser benchmarks looked excellent.

Then I asked ChatGPT to build ast-grep against it.

End-to-End Performance Findings ​

The agent ran that binary across opencode, a real TypeScript repository. At that point, the parser-only benchmark put this Rust implementation roughly 30% ahead of the C runtime.

The application was slower.

How could a parser become thirty percent faster while the application became slower?

The parser benchmark had reused one parser. ast-grep created parsers for thousands of files, then walked every completed tree to extract its outline. The benchmark had measured only the middle of that journey.

The first arena reserved a huge virtual memory region every time a parser was created. It did not immediately consume all that physical memory, which had made the design look harmless. Across a repository, however, that reservation happened thousands of times, and each one cost real work: a fresh round of reserve-and-release syscalls, plus the page-fault and page-table churn behind them, repeated for every file. That churn — not parsing — was the CPU regression on the opencode corpus. I directed ChatGPT to replace the reservation with an ordinary small allocation that grew only when needed.

That removed one problem and exposed another: memory. On the separate TypeScript stress corpus, measured with one ast-grep worker throughout, the arena's early growth strategy kept old blocks alive and pushed peak memory to 1.04 GiB. Getting from there to the final 91.2 MiB took several rounds of arena surgery — including one twist where the memory I kept telling ChatGPT to reclaim turned out not to be the memory actually being wasted. Part 4 has the traces and the culprit; I will not spoil the reveal here.

The completed tree had one more surprise. Compact indexes helped while building it, but ast-grep had to look them up while reading it. Some parser time had simply moved into tree traversal. ChatGPT changed the tree reader to look up each group of children once instead of repeatedly, recovering that cost.

Those repairs — ordinary allocation instead of a per-parser virtual-memory ceremony, and a tree reader that resolves each group of children once — closed the regression, and together with a later round of parser-side tuning they became the numbers at the top of this post: the outline run finishing with 22.2% less user CPU than the C build. The end-to-end failure did not invalidate the parser work. It invalidated the old meaning of “worked.” From then on, a performance result needed to cover parsing, memory, reading the tree, and the complete application lifecycle.

There was no single magic patch behind these results. Some changes saved parser time, some prevented a memory disaster, and others recovered time while reading the completed tree. This overview keeps the principles that connect the individual experiments; the detailed posts take them apart.

Lessons from the AI-Assisted Rewrite ​

At the beginning, AI increased the amount of code a single instruction could set in motion. That was enough to make the rewrite possible and nowhere near enough to make it good.

The early loop looked like this:

text

/goal improve the perf by 20%
        -> a great deal of plausible code
        -> a confusing benchmark
        -> another plausible patch

Later it looked like this:

text

find the expensive work
        -> explain why it happens
        -> change one mechanism
        -> compare with the previous Rust revision
        -> test the complete application
        -> retain, revise, or reject

ChatGPT did not gradually become infallible. I gradually learned enough about the runtime to give it narrower problems, challenge bundled assumptions, and demand evidence at the correct boundary. The segfaulting early speedup, the arena's memory explosion, and the slower application all arrived behind reasonable-looking code and encouraging local results. Profiles and tests had to catch what both of us missed.

By the end, the collaboration had found its proper division of labor. ChatGPT could explore implementation space at a pace I could never match by hand. My job was to keep narrowing the question until profiles, invariants, and end-to-end controls could answer it. Speed made the expedition possible; evidence decided which parts returned.

That is the whole adventure. The remaining posts slow it down:

  1. Rewriting Tree-sitter's C Core in Rust: Migration and Compatibility covers the migration itself, the /goal run and its revert, what this branch deleted, and how the compatibility boundary survived.
  2. Improving Tree-sitter's GLR Algorithm and Memory Layout explains why the parser built a graph for an almost-always-linear workload, then follows the many decisions hidden inside “use an arena.”
  3. Optimizing Tree-sitter for End-to-End ast-grep Performance contains the memory traces, the traversal investigation, the benchmark rules — and a further round of parser-side optimization (lookup indexes, single-action dispatch) driven by the application profile.

The short version is that AI gave me the chance to move a load-bearing wall. The rest of the project was discovering, one benchmark at a time, everything else that wall had been holding up.

At that point, the parser-only benchmark put this Rust implementation roughly 30% ahead of the C runtime.The application was slower.How could a parser become thirty percent faster while the application became slower?The parser benchmark had reused one parser. ast-grep created parsers for thousands of files, then walked every completed tree to extract its outline. The benchmark had measured only the middle of that journey.The first arena reserved a huge virtual memory region every time a parser was created. It did not immediately consume all that physical memory, which had made the design look harmless. Across a repository, however, that reservation happened thousands of times, and each one cost real work: a fresh round of reserve-and-release syscalls, plus the page-fault and page-table churn behind them, repeated for every file. That churn — not parsing — was the CPU regression on the opencode corpus. I directed ChatGPT to replace the reservation with an ordinary small allocation that grew only when needed.That removed one problem and exposed another: memory. On the separate TypeScript stress corpus, measured with one ast-grep worker throughout, the arena's early growth strategy kept old blocks alive and pushed peak memory to 1.04 GiB. Getting from there to the final 91.2 MiB took several rounds of arena surgery — including one twist where the memory I kept telling ChatGPT to reclaim turned out not to be the memory actually being wasted. Part 4 has the traces and the culprit; I will not spoil the reveal here.The completed tree had one more surprise. Compact indexes helped while building it, but ast-grep had to look them up while reading it. Some parser time had simply moved into tree traversal. ChatGPT changed the tree reader to look up each group of children once instead of repeatedly, recovering that cost.Those repairs — ordinary allocation instead of a per-parser virtual-memory ceremony, and a tree reader that resolves each group of children once — closed the regression, and together with a later round of parser-side tuning they became the numbers at the top of this post: the outline run finishing with 22.2% less user CPU than the C build. The end-to-end failure did not invalidate the parser work. It invalidated the old meaning of “worked.” From then on, a performance result needed to cover parsing, memory, reading the tree, and the complete application lifecycle.There was no single magic patch behind these results. Some changes saved parser time, some prevented a memory disaster, and others recovered time while reading the completed tree. This overview keeps the principles that connect the individual experiments; the detailed posts take them apart.Lessons from the AI-Assisted Rewrite ​At the beginning, AI increased the amount of code a single instruction could set in motion. That was enough to make the rewrite possible and nowhere near enough to make it good.The early loop looked like this:text/goal improve the perf by 20% -> a great deal of plausible code -> a confusing benchmark -> another plausible patchLater it looked like this:textfind the expensive work -> explain why it happens -> change one mechanism -> compare with the previous Rust revision -> test the complete application -> retain, revise, or rejectChatGPT did not gradually become infallible. I gradually learned enough about the runtime to give it narrower problems, challenge bundled assumptions, and demand evidence at the correct boundary. The segfaulting early speedup, the arena's memory explosion, and the slower application all arrived behind reasonable-looking code and encouraging local results. Profiles and tests had to catch what both of us missed.By the end, the collaboration had found its proper division of labor. ChatGPT could explore implementation space at a pace I could never match by hand. My job was to keep narrowing the question until profiles, invariants, and end-to-end controls could answer it. Speed made the expedition possible; evidence decided which parts returned.That is the whole adventure. The remaining posts slow it down:Rewriting Tree-sitter's C Core in Rust: Migration and Compatibility covers the migration itself, the /goal run and its revert, what this branch deleted, and how the compatibility boundary survived.Improving Tree-sitter's GLR Algorithm and Memory Layout explains why the parser built a graph for an almost-always-linear workload, then follows the many decisions hidden inside “use an arena.”Optimizing Tree-sitter for End-to-End ast-grep Performance contains the memory traces, the traversal investigation, the benchmark rules — and a further round of parser-side optimization (lookup indexes, single-action dispatch) driven by the application profile.The short version is that AI gave me the chance to move a load-bearing wall. The rest of the project was discovering, one benchmark at a time, everything else that wall had been holding up.

blocks.html_en: Tree-sitter takes source code and produces a syntax tree. Each supported language begins as a grammar definition that Tree-sitter compiles into generated parsing tables and lexer code; when this series says “generated languages,” “generated grammars,” or “generated tables,” it means those artifacts. At runtime, a lexer turns characters into tokens such as identifier, +, and number. The parser then uses the generated table and a stack to decide what each token means.

blocks.html_en: • Use the existing tests as the behavioral oracle. A plausible Rust implementation was not enough; it had to produce the same trees, recovery behavior, navigation results, and public API effects.

sentences.en: Use the existing tests as the behavioral oracle.
sentences.zh: 使用现有的测试作为行为预言。

sentences.en: A plausible Rust implementation was not enough; it had to produce the same trees, recovery behavior, navigation results, and public API effects.
sentences.zh: 一个看似合理的 Rust 实现是不够的；它必须产生相同的树、恢复行为、导航结果和公共 API 效果。

blocks.html_en: • Test the ecosystem, not only handwritten examples. Existing generated grammars and external scanners had to keep working without regeneration or source changes.

sentences.en: Test the ecosystem, not only handwritten examples.
sentences.zh: 测试生态系统，而不仅仅是手写示例。

sentences.en: Existing generated grammars and external scanners had to keep working without regeneration or source changes.
sentences.zh: 现有的生成语法和外部扫描器必须继续工作，而无需重新生成或源更改。

blocks.html_en: • Preserve the binary interface (ABI). Generated language tables, public C functions, layouts, symbols, and calling conventions remained compatible while the implementation behind them changed language.

sentences.en: Preserve the binary interface (ABI).
sentences.zh: 保留二进制接口 (ABI)。

sentences.en: Generated language tables, public C functions, layouts, symbols, and calling conventions remained compatible while the implementation behind them changed language.
sentences.zh: 生成的语言表、公共 C 函数、布局、符号和调用约定保持兼容，而它们背后的实现改变了语言。

blocks.html_en: • Translate before redesigning. The first Rust version intentionally resembled the C control flow so parity failures had a bounded search area.

sentences.en: Translate before redesigning.
sentences.zh: 重新设计之前进行翻译。

sentences.en: The first Rust version intentionally resembled the C control flow so parity failures had a bounded search area.
sentences.zh: 第一个 Rust 版本有意类似于 C 控制流，因此奇偶校验失败具有有限的搜索区域。

blocks.html_en: In one sentence: preserve everything the ecosystem can observe, then make the inside replaceable.

sentences.en: In one sentence: preserve everything the ecosystem can observe, then make the inside replaceable.
sentences.zh: 一言以蔽之：保护生态系统可以观察到的一切，然后使内部可替换。

blocks.html_en: I instructed ChatGPT to translate the runtime one part at a time: basic utilities, tree storage, lexing, the parser stack, tree navigation, and finally the parser loop. The agent read the C and Rust code, wrote patches, fixed compiler errors, ran tests, and investigated mismatches. I supplied the goals, constraints, objections, and decisions. The existing implementation and test suite supplied the answer key.

sentences.en: I instructed ChatGPT to translate the runtime one part at a time: basic utilities, tree storage, lexing, the parser stack, tree navigation, and finally the parser loop.
sentences.zh: 我指示 ChatGPT 一次转换运行时的一部分：基本实用程序、树存储、词法分析、解析器堆栈、树导航，最后是解析器循环。

sentences.en: The agent read the C and Rust code, wrote patches, fixed compiler errors, ran tests, and investigated mismatches.
sentences.zh: 该代理读取 C 和 Rust 代码、编写补丁、修复编译器错误、运行测试并调查不匹配情况。

sentences.en: I supplied the goals, constraints, objections, and decisions.
sentences.zh: 我提供了目标、限制、反对意见和决定。

sentences.en: The existing implementation and test suite supplied the answer key.
sentences.zh: 现有的实施和测试套件提供了答案。

blocks.html_en: This distinction matters. I did not personally type a heroic Rust port and then ask AI to polish the comments. The implementation, profiling, instrumentation, and much of the experimental code were produced by the agent under my direction. Without AI, this project would still be an idea I occasionally mentioned before wisely changing the subject.

sentences.en: This distinction matters.
sentences.zh: 这种区别很重要。

sentences.en: I did not personally type a heroic Rust port and then ask AI to polish the comments.
sentences.zh: 我并没有亲自输入一个英雄般的 Rust 端口，然后让 AI 来润色评论。

sentences.en: The implementation, profiling, instrumentation, and much of the experimental code were produced by the agent under my direction.
sentences.zh: 实施、分析、检测和大部分实验代码都是由代理在我的指导下编写的。

sentences.en: Without AI, this project would still be an idea I occasionally mentioned before wisely changing the subject.
sentences.zh: 如果没有人工智能，这个项目仍然只是我在明智地改变话题之前偶尔提到的一个想法。

blocks.html_en: The C core had become Rust. It compiled. It passed the tests. Existing grammars could use it. This was already the kind of result that had looked impossible when the project was sitting on the shelf.

sentences.en: The C core had become Rust.
sentences.zh: C 核心已变成 Rust。

sentences.en: It compiled.
sentences.zh: 它编译了。

sentences.en: It passed the tests.
sentences.zh: 它通过了测试。

sentences.en: Existing grammars could use it.
sentences.zh: 现有的语法可以使用它。

sentences.en: This was already the kind of result that had looked impossible when the project was sitting on the shelf.
sentences.zh: 这在项目被搁置时就已经是一种看起来不可能的结果了。

blocks.html_en: Naturally, I immediately asked for more.

sentences.en: Naturally, I immediately asked for more.
sentences.zh: 自然，我立即要求更多。

blocks.html_en: Why the First Optimization Attempt Failed ​

sentences.en: Why the First Optimization Attempt Failed ​
sentences.zh: 为什么第一次优化尝试失败​

blocks.html_en: The request was pure vibe coding — one line typed into a /goal command. The process behind it was more careful than that: I directed ChatGPT to use proper profiling tools, understand the runtime's data layouts and ownership, and look for algorithmic changes instead of merely polishing individual instructions. The benchmarks duly crossed the requested line. Then I opened the code and could not follow it. Layers of overlapping AI-generated optimizations sat on top of a mechanical C-to-Rust translation, and soon the parser began segfaulting: no friendly Rust panic, no failed assertion, the process simply left. A parser that is twenty percent faster and occasionally disappears is not an optimization. It is a benchmark with a jump scare.

sentences.en: The request was pure vibe coding — one line typed into a /goal command.
sentences.zh: 该请求是纯粹的氛围编码——在 /goal 命令中输入一行。

sentences.en: The process behind it was more careful than that: I directed ChatGPT to use proper profiling tools, understand the runtime's data layouts and ownership, and look for algorithmic changes instead of merely polishing individual instructions.
sentences.zh: 其背后的过程比这更仔细：我指示 ChatGPT 使用适当的分析工具，了解运行时的数据布局和所有权，并寻找算法更改，而不是仅仅完善单个指令。

sentences.en: The benchmarks duly crossed the requested line.
sentences.zh: 基准适当地跨越了要求的线。

sentences.en: Then I opened the code and could not follow it.
sentences.zh: 然后我打开代码就看不下去了。

sentences.en: Layers of overlapping AI-generated optimizations sat on top of a mechanical C-to-Rust translation, and soon the parser began segfaulting: no friendly Rust panic, no failed assertion, the process simply left.
sentences.zh: AI 生成的重叠优化层位于机械 C 到 Rust 翻译之上，很快解析器就开始出现段错误：没有友好的 Rust 恐慌，没有失败的断言，进程就这样离开了。

sentences.en: A parser that is twenty percent faster and occasionally disappears is not an optimization.
sentences.zh: 解析器速度提高百分之二十并且偶尔会消失并不是一种优化。

sentences.en: It is a benchmark with a jump scare.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人震惊的基准。

blocks.html_en: I reverted the optimization work entirely. The twenty percent went with it, and the performance the project eventually reached came later, from the clean, layered work described below. Part 2 tells this story in full. What matters here is how it reversed the project: I stopped asking ChatGPT to make the pile faster and started asking it to make the system explainable.

sentences.en: I reverted the optimization work entirely.
sentences.zh: 我完全恢复了优化工作。

sentences.en: The twenty percent went with it, and the performance the project eventually reached came later, from the clean, layered work described below.
sentences.zh: 百分之二十随之而来，项目最终达到的性能是后来通过下面描述的干净、分层的工作实现的。

sentences.en: Part 2 tells this story in full.
sentences.zh: 第 2 部分完整讲述了这个故事。

sentences.en: What matters here is how it reversed the project: I stopped asking ChatGPT to make the pile faster and started asking it to make the system explainable.
sentences.zh: 这里重要的是它如何逆转项目：我不再要求 ChatGPT 加快堆放速度，而是开始要求它使系统变得可解释。

blocks.html_en: Second Step: Reduce Scope and Improve Readability ​

sentences.en: Second Step: Reduce Scope and Improve Readability ​
sentences.zh: 第二步：缩小范围并提高可读性​

blocks.html_en: The cleanup had two parts:

sentences.en: The cleanup had two parts:
sentences.zh: 清理工作分为两部分：

blocks.html_en: • delete features and representations outside the target product;

sentences.en: delete features and representations outside the target product;
sentences.zh: 删除目标产品之外的特征和表示；

blocks.html_en: • turn the retained C-style Rust into code whose ownership and control flow could be reasoned about locally.

sentences.en: turn the retained C-style Rust into code whose ownership and control flow could be reasoned about locally.
sentences.zh: 将保留的 C 风格 Rust 转换为可以在本地推理其所有权和控制流的代码。

blocks.html_en: Neither step promised a heroic benchmark. Both were prerequisites for trusting the next one.

sentences.en: Neither step promised a heroic benchmark.
sentences.zh: 这两个步骤都没有承诺英雄的基准。

sentences.en: Both were prerequisites for trusting the next one.
sentences.zh: 两者都是信任下一个的先决条件。

blocks.html_en: Remove Incremental Parsing from the Target Runtime ​

sentences.en: Remove Incremental Parsing from the Target Runtime ​
sentences.zh: 从目标运行时删除增量解析​

blocks.html_en: At first, “rewrite Tree-sitter” implied preserving every feature. Then the target workload forced a better question: preserving it for whom?

sentences.en: At first, “rewrite Tree-sitter” implied preserving every feature.
sentences.zh: 起初，“重写 Tree-sitter”意味着保留每一个功能。

sentences.en: Then the target workload forced a better question: preserving it for whom?
sentences.zh: 然后，目标工作负载引发了一个更好的问题：为谁保留它？

blocks.html_en: Upstream Tree-sitter is famously useful inside editors. A human inserts one character, deletes two more, and expects highlighting to update before the next frame. Incremental parsing lets the runtime reuse the old tree and rebuild only the affected region. In that world, reparsing the complete file after every keystroke is needless work.

sentences.en: Upstream Tree-sitter is famously useful inside editors.
sentences.zh: 上游 Tree-sitter 在编辑器中非常有用。

sentences.en: A human inserts one character, deletes two more, and expects highlighting to update before the next frame.
sentences.zh: 人类插入一个字符，再删除两个字符，并期望突出显示在下一帧之前更新。

sentences.en: Incremental parsing lets the runtime reuse the old tree and rebuild only the affected region.
sentences.zh: 增量解析允许运行时重用旧树并仅重建受影响的区域。

sentences.en: In that world, reparsing the complete file after every keystroke is needless work.
sentences.zh: 在那个世界里，每次击键后重新解析整个文件是不必要的工作。

blocks.html_en: That was not the world of this branch. ast-grep and the AI coding-agent tools I cared about operate on complete file snapshots: an agent reads a file, analyzes or rewrites it, and asks the tool to process the new snapshot. There is no editor-owned syntax tree advancing one keystroke at a time. A fresh parse is not a degraded fallback; it is the normal operation.

sentences.en: That was not the world of this branch.
sentences.zh: 那不是这个分支的世界。

sentences.en: ast-grep and the AI coding-agent tools I cared about operate on complete file snapshots: an agent reads a file, analyzes or rewrites it, and asks the tool to process the new snapshot.
sentences.zh: ast-grep 和我关心的 AI 编码代理工具对完整的文件快照进行操作：代理读取文件，分析或重写它，并要求工具处理新快照。

sentences.en: There is no editor-owned syntax tree advancing one keystroke at a time.
sentences.zh: 不存在编辑器拥有的语法树，一次推进一个击键。

sentences.en: A fresh parse is not a degraded fallback; it is the normal operation.
sentences.zh: 全新的解析并不是降级的后备；而是一种新的解析。这是正常操作。

blocks.html_en: So I decided to remove incremental old-tree reuse and instructed ChatGPT to do it. The public parameter remains for compatibility, but this runtime parses fresh. The machinery for finding and reusing pieces of the old tree — and it reached into a surprising number of core structures — disappeared from the hot implementation; Part 2 inventories exactly what went.

sentences.en: So I decided to remove incremental old-tree reuse and instructed ChatGPT to do it.
sentences.zh: 因此，我决定删除增量旧树重用，并指示 ChatGPT 这样做。

sentences.en: The public parameter remains for compatibility, but this runtime parses fresh.
sentences.zh: 保留公共参数是为了兼容性，但此运行时解析新鲜。

sentences.en: The machinery for finding and reusing pieces of the old tree — and it reached into a surprising number of core structures — disappeared from the hot implementation; Part 2 inventories exactly what went.
sentences.zh: 寻找和重用旧树碎片的机制——它涉及数量惊人的核心结构——从热门实施中消失了；第 2 部分盘点到底发生了什么。

blocks.html_en: A second, separate scope cut rode along with it: native loading of Wasm-compiled grammars. Tree-sitter can compile a grammar to WebAssembly and load it at runtime — a capability distinct from the browser Wasm build, which stayed. Native tools set this project's performance target, and runtime Wasm grammar loading was not part of that workload.

sentences.en: A second, separate scope cut rode along with it: native loading of Wasm-compiled grammars.
sentences.zh: 第二个单独的范围削减随之而来：Wasm 编译语法的本机加载。

sentences.en: Tree-sitter can compile a grammar to WebAssembly and load it at runtime — a capability distinct from the browser Wasm build, which stayed.
sentences.zh: Tree-sitter 可以将语法编译为 WebAssembly 并在运行时加载它——这一功能与保留下来的浏览器 Wasm 构建不同。

sentences.en: Native tools set this project's performance target, and runtime Wasm grammar loading was not part of that workload.
sentences.zh: 本机工具设置了该项目的性能目标，运行时 Wasm 语法加载不是该工作负载的一部分。

blocks.html_en: This is not a proposal that upstream Tree-sitter should abandon incremental parsing. It is a product decision for a narrower runtime aimed at file-at-a-time analysis and agent tooling. If this branch returns to interactive editor use, the decision must be reopened. That was the rule: delete only behind a declared boundary, never because a feature happened to be inconvenient.

sentences.en: This is not a proposal that upstream Tree-sitter should abandon incremental parsing.
sentences.zh: 这并不是建议上游 Tree-sitter 应该放弃增量解析。

sentences.en: It is a product decision for a narrower runtime aimed at file-at-a-time analysis and agent tooling.
sentences.zh: 这是针对更窄的运行时间的产品决策，旨在一次文件分析和代理工具。

sentences.en: If this branch returns to interactive editor use, the decision must be reopened.
sentences.zh: 如果此分支返回到交互式编辑器使用，则必须重新做出决定。

sentences.en: That was the rule: delete only behind a declared boundary, never because a feature happened to be inconvenient.
sentences.zh: 这就是规则：只在声明的边界后面删除，永远不要因为某个功能碰巧不方便而删除。

blocks.html_en: Deletion turned out to be the first real optimization technique: remove work whose use case has already left the building.

sentences.en: Deletion turned out to be the first real optimization technique: remove work whose use case has already left the building.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，删除是第一个真正的优化技术：删除用例已经离开建筑物的工作。

blocks.html_en: Refactor the Retained Runtime for Maintainability ​

sentences.en: Refactor the Retained Runtime for Maintainability ​
sentences.zh: 重构保留的运行时以实现可维护性​

blocks.html_en: A line-by-line translation is only readable if the reader already knows the original line by line. I instructed ChatGPT to break the monolithic, pointer-heavy port into more idiomatic internal Rust—without making the ABI-facing types “idiomatic” in ways that would break existing grammars.

sentences.en: A line-by-line translation is only readable if the reader already knows the original line by line.
sentences.zh: 仅当读者已经逐行了解原文时，逐行翻译才可读。

sentences.en: I instructed ChatGPT to break the monolithic, pointer-heavy port into more idiomatic internal Rust—without making the ABI-facing types “idiomatic” in ways that would break existing grammars.
sentences.zh: 我指示 ChatGPT 将单一的、大量指针的端口打破为更惯用的内部 Rust，而不会以破坏现有语法的方式使面向 ABI 的类型变得“惯用”。

blocks.html_en: The cleanup was less a redesign than a long series of small promotions. Internal raw-pointer parameters became references or slices wherever their lifetimes were local and provable; a sentinel pointer meaning “no node here” became an honest Option. Out-parameters turned into return values where the C ABI did not demand them, large modules split by responsibility so mutation sat next to the state it changed, and the dense tricks that had to stay — compact indexes into the tree, pointer arithmetic — were hidden behind narrow, named operations. Where compatibility was real, the code stayed deliberately ugly: generated-language layouts and exported functions remained C-shaped, because another binary had already committed to that shape.

sentences.en: The cleanup was less a redesign than a long series of small promotions.
sentences.zh: 这次清理与其说是重新设计，不如说是一系列小型促销活动。

sentences.en: Internal raw-pointer parameters became references or slices wherever their lifetimes were local and provable; a sentinel pointer meaning “no node here” became an honest Option.
sentences.zh: 内部原始指针参数成为引用或切片，只要它们的生命周期是本地的且可证明的；意味着“这里没有节点”的哨兵指针成为一个诚实的选项。

sentences.en: Out-parameters turned into return values where the C ABI did not demand them, large modules split by responsibility so mutation sat next to the state it changed, and the dense tricks that had to stay — compact indexes into the tree, pointer arithmetic — were hidden behind narrow, named operations.
sentences.zh: 输出参数变成了 C ABI 不需要的返回值，大型模块按责任划分，因此突变位于它更改的状态旁边，而必须保留的密集技巧（树中的紧凑索引、指针算术）隐藏在狭窄的命名操作后面。

sentences.en: Where compatibility was real, the code stayed deliberately ugly: generated-language layouts and exported functions remained C-shaped, because another binary had already committed to that shape.
sentences.zh: 在兼容性真实的地方，代码故意保持丑陋：生成的语言布局和导出的函数仍然是 C 形的，因为另一个二进制文件已经提交了该形状。

blocks.html_en: That cleanup made questions answerable: Who owns this piece of the tree? Can this reference survive when its storage grows? Why does one reduction create a temporary parser state only to delete it immediately?

sentences.en: That cleanup made questions answerable: Who owns this piece of the tree?
sentences.zh: 这次清理工作让问题有了答案：谁拥有这棵树的这一部分？

sentences.en: Can this reference survive when its storage grows?
sentences.zh: 当存储空间增加时，该引用能否继续存在？

sentences.en: Why does one reduction create a temporary parser state only to delete it immediately?
sentences.zh: 为什么一次归约会创建一个临时解析器状态，然后立即将其删除？

blocks.html_en: The important output was not prettier syntax. It was a runtime organized well enough that a segfault, invariant failure, or suspicious allocation had an address in the architecture.

sentences.en: The important output was not prettier syntax.
sentences.zh: 重要的输出并不是更漂亮的语法。

sentences.en: It was a runtime organized well enough that a segfault, invariant failure, or suspicious allocation had an address in the architecture.
sentences.zh: 这是一个组织得足够好的运行时，段错误、不变故障或可疑分配在架构中都有一个地址。

blocks.html_en: GLR and Memory-Layout Optimizations ​

sentences.en: GLR and Memory-Layout Optimizations ​
sentences.zh: GLR 和内存布局优化​

blocks.html_en: Once I could understand the runtime, I directed ChatGPT back toward reduction — the “reduce” from the architecture section above, and the operation the parser performs constantly.

sentences.en: Once I could understand the runtime, I directed ChatGPT back toward reduction — the “reduce” from the architecture section above, and the operation the parser performs constantly.
sentences.zh: 一旦我能够理解运行时，我就将 ChatGPT 引导回减少 - 上面架构部分的“减少”，以及解析器不断执行的操作。

blocks.html_en: That small operation touches both major data structures. It removes the children from the parser's working stack, then stores them under a new parent in the syntax tree. The profile showed that Tree-sitter was doing much more work around those children than the ordinary case required.

sentences.en: That small operation touches both major data structures.
sentences.zh: 这个小操作涉及两个主要的数据结构。

sentences.en: It removes the children from the parser's working stack, then stores them under a new parent in the syntax tree.
sentences.zh: 它从解析器的工作堆栈中删除子级，然后将它们存储在语法树中的新父级下。

sentences.en: The profile showed that Tree-sitter was doing much more work around those children than the ordinary case required.
sentences.zh: 档案显示，树木保姆在这些孩子周围所做的工作比普通案件所需的要多得多。

blocks.html_en: The successful changes eventually fell into four simple principles:

sentences.en: The successful changes eventually fell into four simple principles:
sentences.zh: 成功的变革最终归结为四个简单的原则：

blocks.html_en: • Avoid work for uncommon cases. About 99% of the observed parser stack was one straight path, so the parser no longer builds a graph until the input actually forks. Work needed mainly for editing is also kept out of a fresh parse when possible.

sentences.en: Avoid work for uncommon cases.
sentences.zh: 避免罕见情况的工作。

sentences.en: About 99% of the observed parser stack was one straight path, so the parser no longer builds a graph until the input actually forks.
sentences.zh: 观察到的解析器堆栈中大约 99% 是一条直线路径，因此解析器在输入实际分叉之前不再构建图。

sentences.en: Work needed mainly for editing is also kept out of a fresh parse when possible.
sentences.zh: 如果可能的话，主要用于编辑所需的工作也不会进行新的解析。

blocks.html_en: • Make allocation cheap, and indexes small. Asking the general-purpose allocator for every internal syntax node is expensive. An arena obtains a growing block and serves many nodes from it. Separately, compact indexes reduce the bytes moved between the parser stack and the tree.

sentences.en: Make allocation cheap, and indexes small.
sentences.zh: 使分配成本降低，索引变小。

sentences.en: Asking the general-purpose allocator for every internal syntax node is expensive.
sentences.zh: 向通用分配器询问每个内部语法节点的成本很高。

sentences.en: An arena obtains a growing block and serves many nodes from it.
sentences.zh: 竞技场获得一个不断增长的块并从中服务许多节点。

sentences.en: Separately, compact indexes reduce the bytes moved between the parser stack and the tree.
sentences.zh: 另外，紧凑索引减少了解析器堆栈和树之间移动的字节。

blocks.html_en: • Do repeated work once. The parser prepares common grammar lookups ahead of time, and the tree reader avoids looking up the same children repeatedly.

sentences.en: Do repeated work once.
sentences.zh: 重复工作一次。

sentences.en: The parser prepares common grammar lookups ahead of time, and the tree reader avoids looking up the same children repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 解析器提前准备常见的语法查找，并且树读取器避免重复查找相同的子项。

blocks.html_en: • Give the simplest cases a short path. One parser action is handled directly, and ordinary ASCII input avoids the full character-decoding path. The complete fallback remains available whenever the simple path does not apply.

sentences.en: Give the simplest cases a short path.

content_html_zh:
第 1 部分（共 4 部分）——完整的冒险

ast-grep 用 Rust 重写了 Tree-sitter 的 C 核心，并由 AI 编写代码。 新的核心解析速度更快，读取完整的树更快，ast-grep 本身也更快。 （标题中的“30%”是仅解析器的数字；端到端，ast-grep 的运行速度大约快 22%。）

源存储库：HerringtonDarkholme/tree-sitter。

在数字之前有两个简短的介绍。 ast-grep——本博客所属的结构代码搜索工具——通过语法而不是文本搜索代码，因此它涉及的每个文件都必须首先成为语法树。 Tree-sitter 是构建该树的解析器框架：您给它一个语法定义，它会为该语言生成一个快速解析器。 它诞生于编辑器世界，现在为一个庞大的语法和工具生态系统提供动力。

性能和峰值 RSS。 吞吐量已标准化，因此未修改的 C 构建（“C/正常”）得分为 100；越高越好。 RSS 是峰值驻留内存，原始解析行将其显示为一个范围，因为它在基准测试的语言固定装置中有所不同。 大纲行是 ast-grep 的实际工作量：解析存储库中的每个文件，然后遍历每个完成的树以提取结构大纲。

基准C/正常Rust不同之处
原始解析吞吐量：100RSS：8.48–21.41 MiB吞吐量：129.74RSS：8.42–25.70 MiB+29.74% 吞吐量+20.0% RSS 上限
树遍历吞吐量：100RSS：20.38 MiB吞吐量：110.16RSS：22.20 MiB+10.16% 吞吐量+8.9% RSS
完整的 ast-grep 大纲用户 CPU：1.233 sRSS：26.52 MiB用户 CPU：0.960 sRSS：34.43 MiB−22.2% 用户 CPU+29.8% RSS

Rust 赢得了所有解析器和遍历装置，并且 ast-grep 产生了完全相同的轮廓。 内存是一个权衡：Rust 构建在 ast-grep 运行中多使用了大约 8 MiB。 在更大的 TypeScript 压力语料库（TypeScript 编译器存储库的测试基线树、该项目的内存折磨测试）上，其峰值为 91.2 MiB。 这个数字是一种胜利，而不是一种忏悔：在项目早期，同一语料库的峰值超过 1 GiB。

结果并不是对上游 Tree-sitter 进行 1:1 替代。 它是为分析完整文件快照的 AI 编码代理构建的更窄的运行时：

  • 现有的生成语言和解析器保持兼容。
  • WebAssembly 编译语言的本机加载和增量旧树重用已被删除。
  • 兼容性仍然需要许多原始指针和不安全块。

该边界使语法生态系统对代理编码保持有用，同时删除目标工作负载不需要的特定于编辑器的机制。

这就是结局。 到达那里是另一回事。

为什么要重写 Tree-sitter？ ​

每一次认真的 ast-grep 性能调查最终都会到达同一个地方：Tree-sitter。

ast-grep 可以使其规则更快。 它可以修剪工作、缓存配置并避免访问不相关的语法。 但每个文件仍然必须首先成为语法树，Tree-sitter 构建了该树。 解析器既是基础，也越来越成为天花板。

多年来我一直梦想着重写或深度优化它。 这个梦通常会持续到我打开运行时为止。 有成熟的 C 实现、二进制兼容性、外部扫描器、错误恢复、增量解析、二义性语法、多种语言绑定，以及不破坏建立在其之上的庞大语法生态系统的小问题。

对于一个人来说，这不是一个周末项目。 这是一项需要头文件的艰巨任务。

所以什么也没发生。

然后，人工智能辅助重写尝试开始随处可见，其中包括 Bun、pgrust 和 Roc。 他们没有证明重写 Tree-sitter 是明智的，使运行时间更小，或者使解析器理论不那么奇怪。 他们表明，这项实验已经变得足够便宜，一个人就可以尝试，这给了我足够的筹码来提出不合理的问题，并在十年结束之前得到答案。

所以我指示 ChatGPT 用 Rust 重写 Tree-sitter 的 C 核心。 该项目从兼容性优先的翻译，通过快速但不可读的优化尝试，转向更简单的运行时和真正的解析器增益——结果发现更快的解析器仍然可能使 ast-grep 变慢。

本文的其余部分将讲述这个旅程：什么有效，什么必须恢复，以及如何将解析器基准测试的胜利转变为应用程序的胜利。

Tree-sitter 的解析架构​

Tree-sitter 获取源代码并生成语法树。 每种受支持的语言都以语法定义开始，Tree-sitter 将其编译为生成的解析表和词法分析器代码；当本系列提到“生成的语言”、“生成的语法”或“生成的表”时，它指的是那些工件。 在运行时，词法分析器将字符转换为标记，例如标识符、+ 和数字。 然后解析器使用生成的表和堆栈来决定每个标记的含义。

大多数时候，该表请求以下两个操作之一：

  • shift：消耗一个token并将其压入解析器堆栈；
  • 减少：认识到几个语法片段形成了一个更大的语法规则，用一个父代替换它们，然后继续。

如果每个表条目都有一个有效答案，则解析器可以使用一个堆栈跟踪一个历史记录。 这就是普通的LR情况。 编程语言语法偶尔会出现真正的冲突：在额​​外的输入揭示哪种解释有效之前，多个操作可能仍然有效。

因此，Tree-sitter 使用广义 LR (GLR)。 它可以同时跟踪多个历史，同时在图结构堆栈中共享它们共同的过去。 想象一条可以短暂分叉然后再次合并的路。 当语法有歧义时，图表是必要的。 当解析器为一条保持笔直的道路构建图形机制时，它就没有那么迷人了。

另一个中心对象是子树。 移动的令牌变成叶子；缩减将子级合并到内部语法节点中。 这些值在解析期间创建，在堆栈历史中共享，作为最终树发布，由 ast-grep 遍历，并最终发布。 仅优化他们的出生而忽略这一生的其余部分将在以后产生相当昂贵的教训。

对于概述来说，这已经足够了。

第一步：在 Rust 中保留 C 行为

第一个目标不是优雅。 这是平等的。

重写合约故意保守：

  • 使用现有的测试作为行为预言。 一个看似合理的 Rust 实现是不够的；它必须产生相同的树、恢复行为、导航结果和公共 API 效果。
  • 测试生态系统，而不仅仅是手写示例。 现有的生成语法和外部扫描器必须继续工作，而无需重新生成或源更改。
  • 保留二进制接口 (ABI)。 生成的语言表、公共 C 函数、布局、符号和调用约定保持兼容，而它们背后的实现改变了语言。
  • 重新设计之前进行翻译。 第一个 Rust 版本有意类似于 C 控制流，因此奇偶校验失败具有有限的搜索区域。

一言以蔽之：保护生态系统可以观察到的一切，然后使内部可替换。

我指示 ChatGPT 一次转换运行时的一部分：基本实用程序、树存储、词法分析、解析器堆栈、树导航，最后是解析器循环。 该代理读取 C 和 Rust 代码、编写补丁、修复编译器错误、运行测试并调查不匹配情况。 我提供了目标、限制、反对意见和决定。 现有的实施和测试套件提供了答案。

这种区别很重要。 我并没有亲自输入一个英雄般的 Rust 端口，然后让 AI 来润色评论。 实施、分析、检测和大部分实验代码都是由代理在我的指导下编写的。 如果没有人工智能，这个项目仍然只是我在明智地改变话题之前偶尔提到的一个想法。

C 核心已变成 Rust。 它编译了。 它通过了测试。 现有的语法可以使用它。 这在项目被搁置时就已经是一种看起来不可能的结果了。

自然，我立即要求更多。

为什么第一次优化尝试失败​

该请求是纯粹的氛围编码——在 /goal 命令中输入一行。 其背后的过程比这更仔细：我指示 ChatGPT 使用适当的分析工具，了解运行时的数据布局和所有权，并寻找算法更改，而不是仅仅完善单个指令。 基准适当地跨越了要求的线。 然后我打开代码就看不下去了。 AI 生成的重叠优化层位于机械 C 到 Rust 翻译之上，很快解析器就开始出现段错误：没有友好的 Rust 恐慌，没有失败的断言，进程就这样离开了。 解析器速度提高百分之二十并且偶尔会消失并不是一种优化。 这是一个令人震惊的基准。

我完全恢复了优化工作。 百分之二十随之而来，项目最终达到的性能是后来通过下面描述的干净、分层的工作实现的。 第 2 部分完整讲述了这个故事。 这里重要的是它如何逆转项目：我不再要求 ChatGPT 加快堆放速度，而是开始要求它使系统变得可解释。

第二步：缩小范围并提高可读性​

清理工作分为两部分：

  1. 删除目标产品之外的特征和表示；
  2. 将保留的 C 风格 Rust 转换为可以在本地推理其所有权和控制流的代码。

这两个步骤都没有承诺英雄的基准。 两者都是信任下一个的先决条件。

从目标运行时删除增量解析​

起初，“重写 Tree-sitter”意味着保留每一个功能。 然后，目标工作负载引发了一个更好的问题：为谁保留它？

上游 Tree-sitter 在编辑器中非常有用。 人类插入一个字符，再删除两个字符，并期望突出显示在下一帧之前更新。 增量解析允许运行时重用旧树并仅重建受影响的区域。 在那个世界里，每次击键后重新解析整个文件是不必要的工作。

那不是这个分支的世界。 ast-grep 和我关心的 AI 编码代理工具对完整的文件快照进行操作：代理读取文件，分析或重写它，并要求工具处理新快照。 不存在编辑器拥有的语法树，一次推进一个击键。 全新的解析并不是降级的后备；而是一种新的解析。这是正常操作。

因此，我决定删除增量旧树重用，并指示 ChatGPT 这样做。 保留公共参数是为了兼容性，但此运行时解析新鲜。 寻找和重用旧树碎片的机制——它涉及数量惊人的核心结构——从热门实施中消失了；第 2 部分盘点到底发生了什么。

第二个单独的范围削减随之而来：Wasm 编译语法的本机加载。 Tree-sitter 可以将语法编译为 WebAssembly 并在运行时加载它——这一功能与保留下来的浏览器 Wasm 构建不同。 本机工具设置了该项目的性能目标，运行时 Wasm 语法加载不是该工作负载的一部分。

这并不是建议上游 Tree-sitter 应该放弃增量解析。 这是针对更窄的运行时间的产品决策，旨在一次文件分析和代理工具。 如果此分支返回到交互式编辑器使用，则必须重新做出决定。 这就是规则：只在声明的边界后面删除，永远不要因为某个功能碰巧不方便而删除。

事实证明，删除是第一个真正的优化技术：删除用例已经离开建筑物的工作。

重构保留的运行时以实现可维护性​

仅当读者已经逐行了解原文时，逐行翻译才可读。 我指示 ChatGPT 将单一的、大量指针的端口打破为更惯用的内部 Rust，而不会以破坏现有语法的方式使面向 ABI 的类型变得“惯用”。

这次清理与其说是重新设计，不如说是一系列小型促销活动。 内部原始指针参数成为引用或切片，只要它们的生命周期是本地的且可证明的；意味着“这里没有节点”的哨兵指针成为一个诚实的选项。 输出参数变成了 C ABI 不需要的返回值，大型模块按责任划分，因此突变位于它更改的状态旁边，而必须保留的密集技巧（树中的紧凑索引、指针算术）隐藏在狭窄的命名操作后面。 在兼容性真实的地方，代码故意保持丑陋：生成的语言布局和导出的函数仍然是 C 形的，因为另一个二进制文件已经提交了该形状。

这次清理工作让问题有了答案：谁拥有这棵树的这一部分？ 当存储空间增加时，该引用能否继续存在？ 为什么一次归约会创建一个临时解析器状态，然后立即将其删除？

重要的输出并不是更漂亮的语法。 这是一个组织得足够好的运行时，段错误、不变故障或可疑分配在架构中都有一个地址。

GLR 和内存布局优化​

一旦我能够理解运行时，我就将 ChatGPT 引导回减少 - 上面架构部分的“减少”，以及解析器不断执行的操作。

这个小操作涉及两个主要的数据结构。 它从解析器的工作堆栈中删除子级，然后将它们存储在语法树中的新父级下。 档案显示，树木保姆在这些孩子周围所做的工作比普通案件所需的要多得多。

成功的变革最终归结为四个简单的原则：

  • 避免罕见情况的工作。 观察到的解析器堆栈中大约 99% 是一条直线路径，因此解析器在输入实际分叉之前不再构建图。 如果可能的话，主要用于编辑所需的工作也不会进行新的解析。
  • 使分配成本降低，索引变小。 向通用分配器询问每个内部语法节点的成本很高。 竞技场获得一个不断增长的块并从中服务许多节点。 另外，紧凑索引减少了解析器堆栈和树之间移动的字节。
  • 重复工作一次。 解析器提前准备常见的语法查找，并且树读取器避免重复查找相同的子项。
  • 给最简单的情况一条最短的路径。 直接处理一个解析器操作，普通 ASCII 输入避免了完整的字符解码路径。 当简单路径不适用时，完整的后备仍然可用。

text

ordinary parse: keep one stack path
real ambiguity: switch to the full graph

99% 的数字描述了问题，但没有描述解决方案。 我指示 ChatGPT（这次是在研究模式而不是编码模式）回顾关于广义解析器的学术工作，结果指出了一个较旧的教训：在输入真正需要它之前不要构建通用结构。 竞技场是一个独立的想法，需要自己的实验。 线性堆栈避免了图形记账；竞技场减少了对总分配员的呼叫。 缩小索引是另一种布局选择，并且它不会自动变得更快。 在这些作品收回成本之前，有几个版本丢失了。

重要的结果是：普通解析不再为罕见的歧义和每个内部语法节点的单独分配付出全部代价。

有一段时间，解析器基准看起来非常好。

然后我要求 ChatGPT 针对它构建 ast-grep。

端到端性能调查结果​

该代理跨 opencode（一个真正的 TypeScript 存储库）运行该二进制文件。 那时，仅解析器基准测试表明此 Rust 实现比 C 运行时领先大约 30%。

应用程序速度较慢。

解析器如何变得更快 30%，而应用程序却变得更慢？

解析器基准测试重复使用了一个解析器。 ast-grep 为数千个文件创建了解析器，然后遍历每个完成的树以提取其轮廓。 该基准仅测量了该旅程的中间部分。

每次创建解析器时，第一个竞技场都会保留一个巨大的虚拟内存区域。 它并没有立即消耗所有物理内存，这使得该设计看起来无害。 然而，在一个存储库中，这种保留发生了数千次，并且每一次都需要付出实际的工作：新一轮的保留和释放系统调用，加上它们背后的页面错误和页表搅动，对每个文件重复进行。 这种搅动（不是解析）是开放代码语料库上的 CPU 回归。 我指示 ChatGPT 将预留替换为仅在需要时增长的普通小分配。

这解决了一个问题，但又暴露了另一个问题：内存。 在单独的 TypeScript 压力语料库上，由一名 ast-grep 工作人员全程测量，arena 的早期增长策略使旧块保持活力，并将峰值内存推至 1.04 GiB。 从那里到最终的 91.2 MiB 需要进行几轮竞技场手术 - 包括一个转折，我一直告诉 ChatGPT 回收的内存结果并不是真正被浪费的内存。 第4部分有痕迹和罪魁祸首；我不会破坏这里的揭露。

完成的树还有一个惊喜。 紧凑索引在构建它时有所帮助，但 ast-grep 必须在阅读时查找它们。 一些解析器时间只是转移到树遍历上。 ChatGPT 将树读取器更改为查找每组子项一次而不是重复查找，从而收回了成本。

这些修复——普通分配而不是每个解析器的虚拟内存仪式，以及解析每组子对象一次的树阅读器——关闭了回归，并与后一轮解析器端调整一起，它们成为本文顶部的数字：大纲运行完成时，用户 CPU 比 C 版本少了 22.2%。 端到端失败并没有使解析器工作失效。 它使“有效”的旧含义失效了。 从那时起，性能结果需要涵盖解析、内存、读取树和完整的应用程序生命周期。

这些结果背后没有任何神奇的补丁。 一些更改节省了解析器时间，一些更改防止了内存灾难，另一些则在读取完整的树时恢复了时间。 这个概述保留了连接各个实验的原则；详细的帖子将它们分开。

人工智能辅助重写的经验教训​

一开始，人工智能增加了单条指令可以启动的代码量。 这足以使重写成为可能，但远不足以使其变得更好。

早期的循环如下所示：

text

/goal improve the perf by 20%
        -> a great deal of plausible code
        -> a confusing benchmark
        -> another plausible patch

后来它看起来像这样：

text

find the expensive work
        -> explain why it happens
        -> change one mechanism
        -> compare with the previous Rust revision
        -> test the complete application
        -> retain, revise, or reject

ChatGPT 并没有逐渐变得万无一失。 我逐渐对运行时有了足够的了解，以解决更窄的问题，挑战捆绑的假设，并在正确的边界要求证据。 早期加速的段错误、竞技场的内存爆炸以及较慢的应用程序都出现在看起来合理的代码和令人鼓舞的本地结果的背后。 分析和测试必须找出我们都错过的东西。

最终，双方的合作找到了合适的分工。 ChatGPT 可以以我手动无法比拟的速度探索实施空间。 我的工作是不断缩小问题范围，直到配置文件、不变量和端到端控制能够回答它。 速度使这次探险成为可能；证据决定了哪些零件被退回。

这就是整个冒险。 其余的帖子会减慢速度：

  1. 用 Rust 重写 Tree-sitter 的 C 核心：迁移和兼容性涵盖了迁移本身、/goal 运行及其恢复、该分支删除的内容以及兼容性边界如何保留。
  2. 改进 Tree-sitter 的 GLR 算法和内存布局解释了为什么解析器为几乎总是线性的工作负载构建了一个图表，然后遵循隐藏在“使用竞技场”中的许多决策。
  3. 优化 Tree-sitter 以实现端到端 ast-grep 性能包含内存跟踪、遍历调查、基准测试规则 - 以及由应用程序配置文件驱动的另一轮解析器端优化（查找索引、单操作调度）。

简而言之，人工智能让我有机会移动承重墙。 该项目的其余部分是一次一个基准地发现那堵墙所支撑的其他一切。
